name: Split-Type Aircon
description: The most common type for homes and offices. Consists of an indoor unit mounted high on the wall and an outdoor compressor unit. Quiet, efficient, and available in 0.5hp to 5.0hp+ capacities.
features: Quietest operation among common types (as low as 19dB)
Inverter technology for energy savings of 30-60%
Available with WiFi/smart controls
Easy installation — minimal ductwork needed
pros: Energy-efficient, quiet, wide capacity range, easy to install
cons: Wall-mounted unit may not suit all room aesthetics; needs outdoor space for condenser

name: Window-Type Aircon
description: Self-contained unit installed in a window or through a wall opening. The most affordable option with all components in one chassis — no separate outdoor unit needed.
features: Lowest upfront cost of all types
Self-contained — no outdoor unit or refrigerant piping
Easy to install and remove (ideal for renters)
Available in standard window sizes
pros: Cheapest, simplest installation, portable between rooms
cons: Noisiest type (40-55dB), blocks window, less energy-efficient than split

name: Cassette-Type Aircon
description: Recessed into the ceiling panel with only a grille visible. Distributes air in 4 directions for even cooling across large rooms. The standard for commercial spaces.
features: Invisible — only the grille shows, saves wall/floor space
4-way airflow for even temperature distribution
Available in 1.5hp to 5.0hp capacities
Some models include fresh air intake option
pros: Clean ceiling look, even cooling across large areas, space-saving
cons: Requires drop ceiling, more expensive installation, harder to service

name: Floor-Mounted / Floor-Standing Aircon
description: Indoor unit sits on or near the floor rather than high on a wall. Ideal for rooms with limited wall space, high ceilings, or where ceiling installation isn't practical.
features: Powerful airflow at floor level where people sit
Easier installation in rooms with concrete walls
Available in high-capacity models (2.5hp to 10hp)
Ideal for rooms with high ceilings
pros: Good for high ceilings, easy to service, strong airflow
cons: Takes up floor space, visible unit and piping

name: Ducted / Concealed Aircon
description: Indoor unit is hidden in the ceiling or a closet and connected to rooms via ducts. The ultimate invisible cooling — ideal for offices, hotels, and commercial spaces.
features: Completely hidden — no visible indoor units
Single unit can serve multiple rooms via duct branches
Quietest operation (unit is remote from occupied spaces)
Can integrate with fresh air / ventilation systems
pros: Invisible, quietest, serves multiple rooms, integrates with ventilation
cons: Highest installation cost, requires ceiling space, hardest to retrofit
